Wine headaches ` [Highlight start] usually happen because of alcohol itself combined with compounds in wine—especially red wine—that affect blood vessels, inflammation, or how your body processes alcohol [Highlight end] ` . They can strike quickly (within 30 minutes to a few hours of a small glass) or show up later like a typical hangover.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXKi08_JYJlghBq4AHx68YNRRcbcmbAf0dvzkGVBS_gMYqvC70tXUjrNmf2zuazpsxabmdV0_SwwmIg0tEQoxJFXiA9Sca8dCMV6aXuQUvRfu4qFkPPSCoUtG6eQcXdD5vf0sp3vwg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF182OSm64CMs9ZmKtSFCamflRQxIKAf09QjQDIrMKvzy6YI4Tz9lqwTD_JFVg8pOQpa-T3Jvt4CAVBp_6p5Ojn6K3XL98yaW1rKZ6K472EEQYbDQE0Hi8Hwp2RtjmqYfpNQ3jGecyX-gqNwQOZQQpNqiXSbicF5rajAw0ekO-gmoJSwrWym2BdDA9a3PC)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXszRkICec-pw-yQWPzOyQ11ZPPFrCdtrQy2CYt3IsroAJUuEk773r9qL4prqs0kIoQlJNXWuKrW5rBVjxfayzgc5ylHwYwllYODvA-gEiG8D-IzUNV2eXk4wc9YDptvcbA5f21Zg)

### Common Causes

- **Quercetin and alcohol metabolism:** Quercetin is a natural antioxidant found in grape skins (and at much higher levels in red wine than white). Research from [UC Davis](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF182OSm64CMs9ZmKtSFCamflRQxIKAf09QjQDIrMKvzy6YI4Tz9lqwTD_JFVg8pOQpa-T3Jvt4CAVBp_6p5Ojn6K3XL98yaW1rKZ6K472EEQYbDQE0Hi8Hwp2RtjmqYfpNQ3jGecyX-gqNwQOZQQpNqiXSbicF5rajAw0ekO-gmoJSwrWym2BdDA9a3PC) suggests quercetin can interfere with enzymes that break down alcohol, causing acetaldehyde to build up and trigger headaches, flushing, or nausea—especially in people prone to migraines or with slower alcohol metabolism.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF182OSm64CMs9ZmKtSFCamflRQxIKAf09QjQDIrMKvzy6YI4Tz9lqwTD_JFVg8pOQpa-T3Jvt4CAVBp_6p5Ojn6K3XL98yaW1rKZ6K472EEQYbDQE0Hi8Hwp2RtjmqYfpNQ3jGecyX-gqNwQOZQQpNqiXSbicF5rajAw0ekO-gmoJSwrWym2BdDA9a3PC)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXKi08_JYJlghBq4AHx68YNRRcbcmbAf0dvzkGVBS_gMYqvC70tXUjrNmf2zuazpsxabmdV0_SwwmIg0tEQoxJFXiA9Sca8dCMV6aXuQUvRfu4qFkPPSCoUtG6eQcXdD5vf0sp3vwg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXX2d7aSXgwtUVPL4oCBxrakKMmD1c1buWqmaKv0mKiyEj0cqHY8HujPjGKQyNX_85PHIPbY6SFzKmvdO-hrKBYovu-oUTF2TxSquQIBTgRICsrdRBuSy-vYtYf-QSdYLEE)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF13v0fqFWS_8XmqBD13y_EA9bgSYWhsa-3n08lgJzQXHEiqaiwnPZCrkWlURL_F7hyCsNsJD88fipU78YPRdxhLvoU98zuTY8_jJsKWDM5zkaoyQdXw4RMRz2AVXi21Jt1uGfOZ5lXr1ZWXM0646jdXqqrFL4yKTcXuPlBZ5CZuvNFd_Y0p4ImHUoKQ)
- **Dehydration and blood vessel changes:** Alcohol acts as a diuretic and dilates blood vessels, which can contribute to throbbing head pain, especially if you drink on an empty stomach or consume sugary wines.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXspNzlW4RjqyFY77tJ_oxV-1SpD30dhPw0xXGSrpPrw7M4FuPByybaI5N1TidLQoNxc4THcKH2rWitCIH4C7XgYpm-bI-1z9XN2Yra-e_dYytqNtX4lf6NwugCIW8xqlnXtsXR4c)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_-EoaOvjIhVV1tvZ0UNMtb-02E52_-y_TQZkk3LZVwGQKnqfiZ9PNPVFUdX1u7VIJawS2LCPOnUWSMrf5GBI-1XBYaR1X83dr6BW55eqRkJ1BlxyYApMqIKI8I5NQ-YNs8sA3ZcUGlVH5Sp5kXF91SO4cDU1HYw6hZ1oODU6jA)
- **Tannins, histamines, and tyramine:** Tannins (higher in red wine) may trigger serotonin fluctuations that provoke migraines in sensitive people. Histamines and tyramine can also play a role in inflammation or blood vessel shifts for some individuals. On a [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF16p3tY0XbPj0PO7wdhTCIIiVsO30MjfozIi7m-VpLYibvIhogLkdyu_6pG4AFDPia8mnqzCL_pjkWwz51mcZZgpMf3VbeQRYyOK1eVyxi0ko1l9skEY14SQwBcwgnmoIB5P2iTk2V_G2czvt4vZT-u-cRw3TCmXzlv_FkWdpCAJF2gikiaf8spS-0AO--qHZsGhdw9TCOoTJSX2o7A) thread, opinions are mixed on exact triggers—some users point to biogenic amines like histamine in red, sparkling, or malolactic-fermented wines, while others emphasize dehydration or alcohol itself.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXysbEzSoKLpfMWUEvmlEvdc4Xi5schhNHoXIPuvpv_-5sbP3nLU8plUW5mX3sOa0Xng7UZAI-Nkab7-pwDw5UIp9y_Ku1eJ4hFH4WhxvmqPVM0sTkp0X-sDvNTW5zR2xr27H7n8rq7CEP_hk)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXspNzlW4RjqyFY77tJ_oxV-1SpD30dhPw0xXGSrpPrw7M4FuPByybaI5N1TidLQoNxc4THcKH2rWitCIH4C7XgYpm-bI-1z9XN2Yra-e_dYytqNtX4lf6NwugCIW8xqlnXtsXR4c)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF16p3tY0XbPj0PO7wdhTCIIiVsO30MjfozIi7m-VpLYibvIhogLkdyu_6pG4AFDPia8mnqzCL_pjkWwz51mcZZgpMf3VbeQRYyOK1eVyxi0ko1l9skEY14SQwBcwgnmoIB5P2iTk2V_G2czvt4vZT-u-cRw3TCmXzlv_FkWdpCAJF2gikiaf8spS-0AO--qHZsGhdw9TCOoTJSX2o7A)
- **Sulfites (less likely):** Despite their reputation, sulfites rarely cause headaches for most people, though they can trigger asthma or allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXKi08_JYJlghBq4AHx68YNRRcbcmbAf0dvzkGVBS_gMYqvC70tXUjrNmf2zuazpsxabmdV0_SwwmIg0tEQoxJFXiA9Sca8dCMV6aXuQUvRfu4qFkPPSCoUtG6eQcXdD5vf0sp3vwg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXysbEzSoKLpfMWUEvmlEvdc4Xi5schhNHoXIPuvpv_-5sbP3nLU8plUW5mX3sOa0Xng7UZAI-Nkab7-pwDw5UIp9y_Ku1eJ4hFH4WhxvmqPVM0sTkp0X-sDvNTW5zR2xr27H7n8rq7CEP_hk)

### Ways to Prevent Them
As outlined by the [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXKi08_JYJlghBq4AHx68YNRRcbcmbAf0dvzkGVBS_gMYqvC70tXUjrNmf2zuazpsxabmdV0_SwwmIg0tEQoxJFXiA9Sca8dCMV6aXuQUvRfu4qFkPPSCoUtG6eQcXdD5vf0sp3vwg) , practical steps include:

- **Drink water and eat first:** Pair wine with food and alternate with water to slow alcohol absorption and stay hydrated.
- **Try a different style:** White wine typically has much less quercetin and fewer tannins than bold red wine.
- **Keep track and limit intake:** Smaller amounts and fewer added sugars can reduce the chance of a reaction.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_-EoaOvjIhVV1tvZ0UNMtb-02E52_-y_TQZkk3LZVwGQKnqfiZ9PNPVFUdX1u7VIJawS2LCPOnUWSMrf5GBI-1XBYaR1X83dr6BW55eqRkJ1BlxyYApMqIKI8I5NQ-YNs8sA3ZcUGlVH5Sp5kXF91SO4cDU1HYw6hZ1oODU6jA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXKi08_JYJlghBq4AHx68YNRRcbcmbAf0dvzkGVBS_gMYqvC70tXUjrNmf2zuazpsxabmdV0_SwwmIg0tEQoxJFXiA9Sca8dCMV6aXuQUvRfu4qFkPPSCoUtG6eQcXdD5vf0sp3vwg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF13v0fqFWS_8XmqBD13y_EA9bgSYWhsa-3n08lgJzQXHEiqaiwnPZCrkWlURL_F7hyCsNsJD88fipU78YPRdxhLvoU98zuTY8_jJsKWDM5zkaoyQdXw4RMRz2AVXi21Jt1uGfOZ5lXr1ZWXM0646jdXqqrFL4yKTcXuPlBZ5CZuvNFd_Y0p4ImHUoKQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXspNzlW4RjqyFY77tJ_oxV-1SpD30dhPw0xXGSrpPrw7M4FuPByybaI5N1TidLQoNxc4THcKH2rWitCIH4C7XgYpm-bI-1z9XN2Yra-e_dYytqNtX4lf6NwugCIW8xqlnXtsXR4c)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXX2d7aSXgwtUVPL4oCBxrakKMmD1c1buWqmaKv0mKiyEj0cqHY8HujPjGKQyNX_85PHIPbY6SFzKmvdO-hrKBYovu-oUTF2TxSquQIBTgRICsrdRBuSy-vYtYf-QSdYLEE)

To help narrow down what might be going on, are you noticing headaches mostly after **red wine** or **any type of wine** , and do they start **within an hour** or **the next morning** ? If you have **migraines** or other symptoms like **flushing** or **nasal congestion** , sharing that can also help.

items.title: Common Causes
items.text: Quercetin and alcohol metabolism: Quercetin is a natural antioxidant found in grape skins (and at much higher levels in red wine than white). Research from UC Davis suggests quercetin can interfere with enzymes that break down alcohol, causing acetaldehyde to build up and trigger headaches, flushing, or nausea—especially in people prone to migraines or with slower alcohol metabolism. Dehydration and blood vessel changes: Alcohol acts as a diuretic and dilates blood vessels, which can contribute to throbbing head pain, especially if you drink on an empty stomach or consume sugary wines. Tannins, histamines, and tyramine: Tannins (higher in red wine) may trigger serotonin fluctuations that provoke migraines in sensitive people. Histamines and tyramine can also play a role in inflammation or blood vessel shifts for some individuals. On a Reddit thread, opinions are mixed on exact triggers—some users point to biogenic amines like histamine in red, sparkling, or malolactic-fermented wines, while others emphasize dehydration or alcohol itself. Sulfites (less likely): Despite their reputation, sulfites rarely cause headaches for most people, though they can trigger asthma or allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.
